claim_boundary.supports: In a three-status ledger model (statuses open / control-only / discharged are this node's vocabulary; the register labels each obligation OPEN) with end-to-end DEFINED as all five discharged: by definition the end-to-end claim holds iff every obligation is discharged, equivalently iff every obligation has a control and none is control-only (general over Fin n, instance n=5; Lean); because ControlOnly and Discharged are distinct statuses, a ledger in which every obligation has a passing control and the end-to-end claim fails exists (the register sentence that scoped controls do not discharge has no Lean declaration); one undischarged obligation blocks the claim; replacing position k of the all-Discharged vector by s gives an end-to-end ledger iff s = Discharged (update_sharp), and a monotone raise of the one undischarged position of a ledger completes it (raise_completes); monotone updates never undo the claim; exactly 1 of the 3^5 = 243 vectors is end-to-end (enforced by the checker over the full public input). Source declarations at general scope: the five-flag Boolean AND is the conjunction; the symmetrised adjacency adj u v || adj v u of a finite window is false iff adj u v and adj v u are both false, and windows with opposite orientation have the same symmetrisation (n=2 countermodel), with no source-to-WDP transition map constructed (that is O02); for all naturals q>0 and p, p*p <> 2*q*q (the source witness checks only q in 1..4, p in 1..6), the arithmetic core of GEN-WDP-68, not progress on O04. The columns upgrades, completing_upgrades, prefix_order and node_reading of the table are native definitions without Lean counterparts.
claim_boundary.does_not_support: That any of O01..O05 is discharged, dischargeable or refutable; the truth of any end-to-end bridge claim; any independent semantics of "end-to-end" beyond the definitional conjunction; that the register status of O01..O05 is control-only: the register labels each OPEN, and Open/ControlOnly/Discharged and the all-ControlOnly vector 11111 are this node's reading of the node statement (scoped controls done, end-to-end not); that no_sq_eq_two_sq bears on O04; the programme order as a logical dependency; Hilbert, Born, scalar or governance choices; any physical or institutional interpretation.
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: In a three-status ledger model in which end-to-end is defined as all five discharged, scoped controls passing for all five obligations do not make the end-to-end claim hold, which holds exactly when all five are discharged; the node reading (all five control-only) is therefore not end-to-end; ledger bookkeeping only, no obligation is discharged.
claim_boundary.next_test: For O02, the only concrete candidate map in hand is the symmetrised adjacency of a finite window: choose an orientation-sensitive source transition system on FiniteGenesisWindow and prove or refute that wdpPairDefect is a preservation-and-reflection morphism for it (pairDefect_forgets_orientation already refutes it for orientation-sensitive transitions); record the outcome as the first falsifier on the O02 row.

second_review.notes: Cold read of run 20261021T175809Z_staged. The Lean module (WdpBridgeObligations.lean) states what the profile says and now says so explicitly in its header: Status {Open, ControlOnly, Discharged} is invented vocabulary (the register, genesis_bridge_register.md rows O01-O05, literally says OPEN and never 'control-only'; I re-read lines 87-91); EndToEnd := every obligation Discharged is a definition, so endToEnd_iff_count, endToEnd_five, endToEnd_iff_controls_and_no_control, control_only_not_discharged and endToEnd_unique are bookkeeping; update_sharp (all-Discharged vector with position k replaced), raise_completes (monotone raise of the single non-discharged position) and endToEnd_mono are the only statements with a little structure; bool_and_iff, pairDefect_preserves_and_reflects (Bool.or_eq_false_iff) and pairDefect_forgets_orientation (n=2 countermodel) are small source re-statements; no_sq_eq_two_sq is a correct strong induction (all q>0, all p) and is labelled as the arithmetic core of GEN-WDP-68, not O04. Checker: independent (counts by filtering, programme order as a pairwise implication, upgrade counts by simulating every strict single-position update, producer uses closed forms), strict types, exact key set, and it now enforces cases == all 243 vectors in order and exactly one end-to-end record, unconditionally. Earlier pass (a): all eight amendments are in the final text (definitional wording, update_sharp / raise_completes wording, symmetrised-adjacency wording, no_sq_eq_two_sq wording, register-literal OPEN reading in does_not_support, narrowest_claim prefix, next_test; the quoted-conjunct fix lives in the operad relation text, which I did not re-read), the 00000 'register_literal_reading', 22211, 22222-not-end-to-end, 22200 and 00000-controls near misses were added (12 semantic mutants), the public-input completeness check was added, and raise_completes was added as a Lean anchor. (b) No new overclaim or weakened check from the rebuild; the only hard-coded value in the checker is node_reading = (v == [1,1,1,1,1]), which is the declared modelling reading and is exercised by two mutants (node_reading_is_end_to_end, register_literal_reading). (c) Residual issues the earlier pass did not raise or that the rebuild left: (1) the profile says the columns 'upgrades, completing_upgrades, prefix_order and node_reading are native definitions without Lean counterparts' while supports cites raise_completes for completing_upgrades and the Lean header says 'only raise_completes, prefixOrder_of_endToEnd have Lean counterparts'; the true state is: raise_completes proves one direction (one undischarged position, raised, completes); the converse (two or more undischarged positions: no single raise completes, i.e. completing_upgrades = 0) and the exact counts are native only, and Lean raise is non-strict while the native upgrade count is strict (s > v[k]); say so. (2) No mutant targets the skip step 22220 completing_upgrades = 0 (claiming an Open obligation cannot be discharged in one monotone update without passing through ControlOnly); the checker would reject it, but it names a real misreading of the ledger and is cheap to add. (3) next_test is node-owned and falsifiable but its first clause relies on the author's O02 reading ('the only concrete candidate map in hand'); acceptable. (4) DAG: the node is PROVED_LEAN with bottleneck 'None' while its own statement says the five obligations are open and the end-to-end claims are not done; the sealed result proves ledger bookkeeping plus three source side facts and discharges nothing, as the reviewed_target_qualification says. The status should be lowered; I agree with the earlier pass (SOURCE_RECORD).

earlier_pass.notes: The Lean module is honest about being bookkeeping, and the checker is a real second computation (upgrade counts by simulating every strict single-position raise; producer uses closed forms; strict types; exact key sets; duplicate and permutation handling). But what is proved is almost entirely consequences of one definition, EndToEnd v := forall k, v k = Discharged, on a three-constructor status type chosen by the author; the 'finding' that scoped controls do not discharge is true because ControlOnly and Discharged are different constructors. The real content (a scoped control does not discharge an obligation) is a register sentence with no Lean declaration, which the relation text admits. The claim boundary says so in does_not_support but supports and the first sentence of narrowest_claim read as if a mathematical fact were established; label them 'definitional' in the sentence itself. Specific issues. (a) supports 'one discharged update completes it': the anchor update_sharp is about Function.update of the constant-Discharged vector, not about the module's own raise on a ledger with four discharged entries; the equivalence the checker computes (completing_upgrades) has no Lean statement (add raise_completes). (b) 'the genesis-to-WDP pair-defect bridge preserves and reflects defect-freeness': in Lean there is only wdpPairDefect w u v := adj u v || adj v u and Bool.or_eq_false_iff; there is no WDP system and no map to preserve or reflect, so 'bridge', 'preserves' and 'reflects' are names; 'defect' is true exactly when an edge exists. This is the symmetrisation of a relation, and the orientation countermodel is correct (n=2). (c) no_sq_eq_two_sq is correct and stronger than the source (all q>0, all p), but the module labels it 'the O04 rational-scalar obstruction'; the register's O04 text (effect/probability axioms, scalar and Hilbert choices) does not mention sqrt 2: that is GEN-WDP-68, a separate proved row. Its place in this node adds nothing to any obligation. (d) source_reported = 11111: the register rows O01..O05 (genesis_bridge_register.md lines 87-91) are each labelled 'OPEN ... OBLIGATION' and the word control-only does not occur; 'Scoped CONTROL items are done' is a global sentence in the node statement. Reading all five as ControlOnly is the author's interpretation (via the completion audit, which I did not re-read), and the vocabulary Open/ControlOnly/Discharged is invented here: in the register's own words all five are simply open. The checker hard-codes v == [1,1,1,1,1], and the 'theorem-level' assertion that a source_reported record has controls_run true is circular. No mutant covers the alternative reading source_reported = 00000. (e) Generators trace_obligation_cost and carriers EventTrace, ObligationCost, Verdict have no Lean definition in this module, no record in the certificate and no anchor (declare_then_assert_cost_floor is not re-proved here); they are source-only and should be marked so. (f) next_test restates the register row for O01 almost verbatim ('justify or explicitly admit the primitive-to-witness carrier, signature, law and challenge-generation floor ... a proposed stronger floor needs a theorem and a falsifier') and duplicates the first item of does_not_support; it is a research programme, not a test, and its ordering relies on the author's own programme order. DAG: the node is PROVED_LEAN with bottleneck 'None' while its statement says the five obligations are open and the end-to-end claims are not done; the Lean here proves bookkeeping lemmas only. The label PROVED_LEAN should be lowered.
